_comment: Strategic Development Plan 2025–2030, taken from the club's own document. Wording is the committee's; only Australian spelling was normalised. Two corrections were authorised by the club: the senior target reads 'four teams by 2030' rather than 'from two to four' (the club already fields three), and the clubhouse item no longer carries its 2026 date, which has passed. The Financial Plan section and all financial lines are deliberately not published.
title: Strategic plan
summary: Over the five years to 2030 the club aims to consolidate its position as a leading sporting organisation by investing in player development, expanding pathways for juniors and women, enhancing facilities, and strengthening governance and community engagement.

items.name: Expand senior teams
items.detail: Grow to four senior men's teams by 2030, catering for different skill levels and aspirations.

items.name: Elite performance programs
items.detail: Introduce high-performance training squads, led by accredited Level 2 and 3 coaches.

items.name: Leadership pathways
items.detail: Implement a Captaincy Leadership Program to develop future club leaders.

items.name: Player retention
items.detail: Create a strong club culture through mentoring, social engagement and welfare programs addressing mental health, fitness and career development.

items.name: Tournament participation
items.detail: Aim to qualify for regional and state-level competitions to elevate competitive standards.

items.name: Pathway establishment
items.detail: Implement a complete junior player pathway from Woolworths Cricket Blast (ages 5–8) through Under-12s, Under-14s and Under-16s competition cricket.

items.name: School partnerships
items.detail: Forge partnerships with five local schools to run regular cricket clinics and interschool tournaments to boost grassroots participation.

items.name: Coach development
items.detail: Train at least 10 new Level 1 accredited junior coaches by 2027, ensuring age-appropriate, engaging and skill-based coaching.

items.name: Parental involvement
items.detail: Develop a “Parents as Volunteers” strategy including team management, scoring, first aid training and event support.

items.name: Junior academy
items.detail: Establish a Junior Cricket Academy to offer specialised coaching to talented youngsters and provide a clear transition into senior teams.

items.name: Women's teams
items.detail: Launch two women's cricket teams, one social and one competitive, by 2028, competing in local competitions.

items.name: Female participation growth
items.detail: Host annual “Girls Cricket Come & Try Days”, aiming for a 20% year-on-year increase in female registrations.

items.name: Coaching and umpiring pathways
items.detail: Provide subsidised Level 1 coaching and umpiring courses specifically for women involved in the club.

items.name: Inclusive facilities
items.detail: Upgrade club facilities to provide female-friendly change rooms and amenities by 2029.

items.name: Leadership representation
items.detail: Ensure that women occupy at least 30% of positions across the Club Committee and Sub-Committees by 2029.

items.name: Board development
items.detail: Introduce skills-based recruitment for Board positions, ensuring expertise in governance, finance, marketing and cricket operations.

items.name: Sub-committee structure
items.detail: Create Senior, Junior, Women's Cricket, Finance and Facilities sub-committees for better operational focus.

items.name: Policy framework
items.detail: Implement formal governance policies covering safeguarding, diversity and inclusion, financial management, conflict of interest and risk management.

items.name: Volunteer management program
items.detail: Launch a structured volunteer program with role descriptions, induction sessions and annual volunteer awards.

items.name: Compliance alignment
items.detail: Regularly review club policies to ensure alignment with Cricket Australia's Good Governance Framework.

items.name: Clubhouse
items.detail: Obtain a newer council facility in the Cranbourne East, Clyde or Clyde North area, with unisex change rooms, disability access and player lounges. Additional grounds will be required as the number of teams grows.

items.name: Indoor training facility
items.detail: Partner with local private providers to access year-round indoor cricket facilities.

items.name: Volunteer shortages
items.detail: Formal volunteer recruitment and retention programs.

items.name: Player recruitment
items.detail: School engagement, digital marketing and “Come and Try” events.

items.name: Facilities delay
items.detail: Early engagement with local council and grants offices.

items.name: Compliance breaches
items.detail: Annual board and volunteer compliance training.

items.name: Risk register
items.detail: A dynamic Risk Register reviewed quarterly at Board meetings to address emerging risks proactively.

sections.title: Monitoring and evaluation
sections.note: Measured at the end of each playing season.

items.name: Annual strategic review
items.detail: Formal review at the end of each playing season measuring performance against key performance indicators.

items.name: Player growth
items.detail: Increase total registered players by 15% annually.

items.name: Women's teams
items.detail: Launched by Year 2.

items.name: Facilities
items.detail: Upgrade on schedule by Year 3.

items.name: Volunteers
items.detail: Volunteer base growth of 10% annually.

items.name: Mid-term review
items.detail: Comprehensive review in 2027 to recalibrate the plan based on achievements and challenges.
